scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “A torsion-free counterexample to reduced Baum–Connes injectivity” (preprints/A-Torsion-Free-Counterexample-to-Reduced-Baum-Connes-Injectivity-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 285 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 df8d9301aa6d0306), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There exist a finitely generated torsion-free discrete group Ginj, an injective homo- morphism i : Z2 → Ginj, and a class c ∈ H2(BGinj; Z) such that D (Bi)∗ c, [T2 ] E = 1, i∗(β) = 0 in K0(C∗ r Ginj), where β is a rank-zero Bott generator of K0(C∗ r Z2). In particular, h = (Bi)∗[DT2 ] has infinite order in K0(BGinj), while its reduced analytic assembly image is zero. Here [DT2 ] is the spin Dirac K-homology class of the oriented torus.
